main_text.p: τὸν πατέρα ἔχειν καὶ τὸν πάππον. ἀμέλει δεινὸς ¶ ἕλκη ἔχειν ἐν τοῖς ἀντιχνη-μίοις, ¶ φρόςπαίσματα ἐν τοῖς δακτύλοις, ἢ ταῦτα μὴ ἀπεσπόσυ, ἀλλ' ἑαυτὴν ἀπειωνῆμα. ¶ τὰς μαχάλας ἀπειῳδεις ἢ δυσεία ἔχὴν ἄχεις ὅπ πολὺ τῶν πλουρῶν. ἢ τοὺς ὀδόντας μελανὰς ¶ ἐθιομψύοις. ὥστε δυσ-ἐντυχὴς ἐῇ καὶ ἀνδρὸς, ¶ τὰ τοιαῦτα. ἐθίων ἀπομύπ-ᾳν. ῥύειν ἐξάμε-ῳ, ὠροσλαλεῖν, ¶ [illegible, ~12 letters] & patrem & auum fuiffe eis obnoxios. Solet etiam ulcera in tibiis, & in manibus tubercula habens, nullam iis medicinam facere: sed finere donec incurabilia reddantur. Axillas ferarum more hirsutas,pilis magnam laterum partem occupantibus, habet. Dentes verò nigros atque exesos, ut molestus sit & infvavis cum eo congressus. Eidē hæc quoque conveniunt: nares inter comedendum mungere: & quum edere inceperit colloqui: & ex ore quædam emittere:inter bibendum eructare: oleo in balneis uti rancido: idemq; in forum veste amictus quæ sit maculis inquinata, prodibit: quúmque ad arufpi-
ἀπορριπτεῖν δὲ τὸ σῶμα. ἅμα πεῖν, προσερυγγάνειν. ἐ-λαίῳ σαπρῷ ἐν βα-λανείῳ χεῖρας. ἡμά-τιον κηλίδων μεσὸν ἀναβαλόμενον, εἰς ἀγορὰν ἐξῆλθεν. ἢ εἰς ὀρνιθοσπό-σπόπ[?]

page.notes: Greek text is small and partly blurred; many words are uncertain and the accents and ¶ marks are approximate. The final line is cut off at the lower edge and is marked illegible. Doubtful words in the Greek are not all individually flagged, so the transcription should be checked against the scan. The Greek block is printed beneath the Latin column; its lines run out to the left and were read with uncertainty in places, especially the words after "ὀρνιθοσπό-" and the Greek word "χεῖρας". The Greek is marked as a foot note because it stands below the text. Some Latin letters near the line ends are hard to make out and may need checking against the full scan.
